text:
olivia: Morning team — quick handoff before I sign off (~18:30 PT). TL;DR: starting a rolling canary for release 3.4.1 on the dedicated pool, prefetch worker showing intermittent latency spikes, and a low-priority embed batch queued. Details and asks below.

mike: ack. Will watch canary metrics and keep the dashboard open.

olivia: What to watch: route=/generate error rate (dashboard: canary -> route-gen). If errors >2% for 10m, escalate. Fallback to the smaller model is enabled automatically, but that will increase latency.

sophia: I'll tail the prefetch worker logs (worker-4). Noted the spike window 04:00–04:30 UTC. If I see repeated OOM or connection resets I'll open a bug and add the logs to the handoff doc.

jordan: I scheduled the embed job (id 789) at 02:00 PT but set priority=low. If GPU util goes >85% for sustained 5m I'll throttle it further. I'll drop a note in #eng-infra if I need to move nodes.

olivia: Action items (short):
- @mike: monitor canary for the next 30m, ping infra if error rate trends up.
- @sophia: investigate worker-4 logs, confirm whether restart fixed the spike or if it's recurring.
- @jordan: watch GPU util and the embed job; move to background queue if contention.

mike: quick command I'll be running to check canary success ratio:
```
# approximate check
curl -s https://monitoring.internal/api/metrics?query=canary_route_gen_success | jq
```
I'll paste the 5m rolling success pct if it moves.

sophia: FYI I already saw a single OOM at 04:12 UTC and performed a grace restart; CPU was fine. Pushing a small patch to reduce buffer size now.

oncall-bot: Reminder: oncall handover in 6h — next person: jordan. Weekly rota: https://hr.internal/rota

mike: small note — yesterday evening we saw a brief quota bump in eu-central that produced rate-limit 429s for ~8m. It auto-resolved; not related to this canary but worth keeping in mind. I lowered the alert sensitivity back to origin defaults.

olivia: Thanks all. I've pinned the minimal checklist and the kplaybook link in this thread. If nothing else, I'm off — leave escalation to @mike/@jordan. Cheers :wave:
